reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) confirms galvanic corrosion between FCC and σ phases in a CoCrFeNiMo HEA in NaCl, but it does not address the key premise that mechanical wear continuously exposes fresh surfaces to drive this process, nor does it provide any evidence for the effect of an external potential bias or the behavior at 300°C.
premises: Mechanical wear exposes fresh surfaces with inherent electrochemical potential differences between phases
Potential differences between phases (e.g., FCC vs. σ) create localized galvanic cells at phase boundaries
Localized galvanic corrosion at phase boundaries accelerates material removal and weakens the alloy
Suppressing the electrochemical gradient will curb local corrosion and reduce wear acceleration
